episode_title: Ep 296 – Bretton AI CEO Will Lawrence
question: Why are major banks like JPMorgan taking a defensive approach against AI agents while smaller community banks are embracing them?
transcript_excerpt: Large banks like JPMorgan are blocking third-party AI agents to push consumers toward their own proprietary platforms, similar to Amazon blocking Muse and Instinct to promote its Rufus agent. This creates opportunities for community and regional banks to attract high-net-worth individuals who prefer using agents like Instinct and Muse, positioning smaller banks as more open alternatives.

question: How much time can Bretton AI save when automating suspicious activity report submissions for AML compliance?
transcript_excerpt: Teams using Bretton AI can cut down their time to create SARs by 87%, which means analysts can file nine times more suspicious activity reports per person or make each filing significantly cheaper to produce.

episode_title: Ep 296 – Bretton AI CEO Will Lawrence
question: What percentage of global money laundering is currently detected by the financial system?
transcript_excerpt: Only about 1% of total money laundering in the world is currently caught, despite billions of dollars in fines and penalties. This is significant because an estimated $2 to $5 trillion is laundered globally every single year, making detection efforts critical to disrupting criminal economies.

episode_title: Ep 296 – Bretton AI CEO Will Lawrence
question: How should banks customize AI agents for AML compliance when the same activity can be suspicious at one bank but normal at another?
transcript_excerpt: Banks should onboard AI agents the same way they onboard humans: provide context on what the bank does, what products and customers it serves, what normal transaction patterns look like, what has historically been suspicious, and provide the necessary system logins and policy guidelines. Agents learn from this institutional knowledge just like new employees, with feedback loops that allow them to refine their decision-making over time.

episode_title: Ep 296 – Bretton AI CEO Will Lawrence
question: What role does human-in-the-loop oversight play in AI automation for anti-money laundering compliance?
transcript_excerpt: While AI agents can functionally perform AML review better than most humans in terms of quality, speed and consistency, regulators require human oversight for critical decisions. The key is having proper controls, independent validation, and human feedback loops. Banks should use AI to improve efficiency and quality of SARs submission while maintaining human approval before filing, rather than moving directly from an alert to SAR filing without any human intervention.
